en.title: From Vedic ritual landscapes to regional religious cultures
en.summary: Chapter argument. Religious change in early Mithilā–Videha, Vajji and Aṅga was cumulative and plural. Vedic ritual traditions were extended eastward and transformed in the courts of Videha; Buddhist, Jain and other śramaṇa communities then became deeply embedded in the urban and political landscapes of Vaiśālī and Campā; and Mauryan and later monumentality made some sacred memories archaeologically durable.

mai.title: वैदिक अनुष्ठानिक भू-दृश्यसँ क्षेत्रीय धार्मिक संस्कृतिधरि
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “वैदिक अनुष्ठानिक भू-दृश्यसँ क्षेत्रीय धार्मिक संस्कृतिधरि” विषयक धार्मिक परम्परा, पवित्र भूगोल, पर्व आ जीवन-चक्रक ऐतिहासिक रूपान्तरणक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Religious history must begin with overlapping practices rather than modern labels
Four evidence streams have to be controlled before they are combined
The Śatapatha story of Videgha Māthava is a charter of ritual eastward movement
Sadānīrā was a symbolic threshold, but its exact modern identification remains debated

en.title: Buddhism in the social history of Vajji and Videha
en.summary: Chapter argument. Buddhism became socially durable in Vajji and Videha through overlapping networks of mobility, patronage, political encounter, gendered participation, monastic regulation and sacred memory. Vesālī provides the densest combination of discourse, Vinaya and archaeological evidence; MN 91 provides unusually direct textual evidence for the Buddha’s itinerary in Videha and an encounter at Mithilā.

mai.title: वज्जि आ विदेहक सामाजिक इतिहासमे बौद्ध धर्म
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “वज्जि आ विदेहक सामाजिक इतिहासमे बौद्ध धर्म” विषयक धार्मिक परम्परा, पवित्र भूगोल, पर्व आ जीवन-चक्रक ऐतिहासिक रूपान्तरणक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Social history asks how Buddhism was embedded, not merely where the Buddha travelled
Four evidence streams must remain separate before synthesis
Vajji, Videha and Mithilā should not be flattened into modern administrative geography
The Brahmāyu Sutta gives unusually direct Buddhist evidence for Videha and Mithilā

en.title: Jainism and the Vaishali–Videha landscape
en.summary: Chapter argument. Jainism became socially embedded in the Vaiśālī–Videha landscape through disciplined ascetic mobility, repeated rainy-season residence, lay–monastic reciprocity, women’s and men’s participation, elite interaction and later sacred memory. The evidence is strongest when Jain canonical traditions, Buddhist external references, archaeology and later pilgrimage identifications are kept distinct before synthesis.

mai.title: वैशाली-विदेह भू-दृश्यमे जैन धर्म
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “वैशाली-विदेह भू-दृश्यमे जैन धर्म” विषयक धार्मिक परम्परा, पवित्र भूगोल, पर्व आ जीवन-चक्रक ऐतिहासिक रूपान्तरणक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: A landscape history must distinguish remembered association from demonstrable institutional presence
Four evidence streams must be controlled separately before synthesis
The historical Mahāvīra is secure; the exact chronology and biography are not
Kuṇḍagrāma links Mahāvīra to the Vaiśālī–Videha zone, but its exact modern identification remains debated

en.title: Śaiva, Śākta and Vaiṣṇava transformations
en.summary: Chapter argument. Between the late ancient and early medieval centuries, Śaiva, Śākta and Vaiṣṇava traditions became increasingly visible in Mithila, Vajji and Aṅga through image installation, temples, ritual specialists, patronage, sacred water and pilgrimage. The transformation was cumulative rather than a single conversion: Buddhist, Jain, Vedic, household and local practices continued within a poly-religious landscape.

mai.title: शैव, शाक्त आ वैष्णव रूपान्तरण
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “शैव, शाक्त आ वैष्णव रूपान्तरण” विषयक धार्मिक परम्परा, पवित्र भूगोल, पर्व आ जीवन-चक्रक ऐतिहासिक रूपान्तरणक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Transformation is a historical process, not a switch from one religion to another
Four evidence streams must be kept separate before they are combined
The Gupta and post-Gupta centuries intensified iconic and temple-centred worship
Śaivism was not one organisation but a family of ritual and theological formations

en.title: Sacred geography
en.summary: Chapter argument. Sacred geography in Mithila, Vajji and Aṅga was produced cumulatively through remembered narratives, repeated movement, water and route infrastructure, monuments, patronage and later pilgrimage. The chapter separates textual, archaeological, epigraphic and later devotional evidence so that modern holy places are not projected backward as unchanged ancient sites.

mai.title: पवित्र भूगोल
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “पवित्र भूगोल” विषयक धार्मिक परम्परा, पवित्र भूगोल, पर्व आ जीवन-चक्रक ऐतिहासिक रूपान्तरणक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Sacred geography is made through historical practice, not discovered as a timeless map
Four evidence streams must be dated separately before a sacred landscape is reconstructed
The Indian category of tīrtha links crossing, place and social movement
Rivers created both sacred corridors and unstable historical evidence

en.title: Festivals and calendrical culture
en.summary: Chapter argument. Calendrical culture in Mithila, Vajji and Aṅga developed through the interaction of lunar and solar reckoning, seasonal ecology, monastic discipline, specialist astronomy, household ritual and regional festival practice. The chapter distinguishes durable calendrical structures from the much more difficult question of the antiquity of individual festivals, and treats the ritual year as a social technology that coordinates labour, gendered practice, markets, sacred places and institutional…

mai.title: पर्व-त्योहार आ पंचांग-संस्कृति
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “पर्व-त्योहार आ पंचांग-संस्कृति” विषयक धार्मिक परम्परा, पवित्र भूगोल, पर्व आ जीवन-चक्रक ऐतिहासिक रूपान्तरणक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Calendars are social infrastructure, not merely systems for naming dates
Four evidence streams must be kept separate before the ritual year is reconstructed
Early Vedic ritual already required coordination of lunar, solar and seasonal time
The lunar fortnight made recurring observance easy to organise across mobile communities

en.title: Death, ancestors and life-cycle rites
en.summary: Chapter argument. Life-cycle rites do not simply preserve an unchanged religious system from antiquity to the present. They convert biological events—conception, birth, maturation, marriage, ageing and death—into socially recognised transitions, and their forms change with household structure, inheritance, gender, ritual authority, religious affiliation and historical period. Mortuary practice is especially revealing because it brings body, kinship, property, memory and sacred geography together.

mai.title: मृत्यु, पूर्वज आ जीवन-चक्र संस्कार
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “मृत्यु, पूर्वज आ जीवन-चक्र संस्कार” विषयक धार्मिक परम्परा, पवित्र भूगोल, पर्व आ जीवन-चक्रक ऐतिहासिक रूपान्तरणक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Life-cycle rites transform biological events into social transitions
Six evidence problems make mortuary history unusually difficult
The classical list of saṃskāras is itself a historical construction
Rigvedic funerary hymns reveal both cremation and an ancestor-oriented imagination
